brief: JPM's Nov 24 morning note centers on Jensen Huang's reinstatement at NVDA, which the desk reads as removing company-specific uncertainty and triggering a sharp reflex rally (SMH +15%, short covering in crowded names, long-only buying back into NVDA) but introducing new corporate-governance risk from presidential intervention, which JPM argues should weigh on equity multiples over time, especially with a Democratic Congress and a possible 2028 Democratic president. A trading-desk client poll finds most respondents view the bounce as a bear-market rally (a dead-cat bounce) rather than a sustainable low, though some expect short-covering to extend into a long chase and CTA buying. JPM's house view returns to Tactically Cautious, comparing the setup to 2018's faded late-year bounce, while flash PMIs point to resilient ~3% Q4 GDP growth that should push Fed-hike expectations back toward three consecutive 25bp hikes from December 2026 to March 2027. Separately, a D1 thematic piece argues the quality rally is maturing and recommends going long high-interest-coverage stocks versus short low-interest-coverage stocks. Dubravko's standalone note (published Nov 6) reiterates an 8,000 year-end-2026 SPX target with several sector trade ideas.
